newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay's economic plans for Thailand seen on track.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay's economic plans for Thailand seen on track.

text.p: Bankers and economists on Thursday voiced support for Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on his recent decisions to cut the national budget and boost stability of financial institutions through capital hikes and higher debt provisions.
Chartsiri Sophonpanich, president of Bangkok Bank Plc, told reporters that Amnuay's conservative policy would help rectify economic problems in the long run provided it could be sustained.
"His current economic measures are on the right track. Although they may be bitter pills, we sometimes do not have much choices," he told reporters.
The banker said he would disagree with any government move to replace Amnuay or his economic team, saying such changes would disrupt essential policy continuity at the expense of national interest.

Chalongphob Susangkarn, president of Thailand Development and Research Institute, said he agreed with Amnuay's move to trim national budget by 99 billion baht ($3.8 billion) during the current fiscal year ending September 30, 1997, in order to help curb current account deficit.

He said, however, that the government needs to further clarify its measures this week to boost stability of the financial sector if it seeks to win more public support. (US$1 = 25.8 baht) -- Bangkok newsroom (662)-6520642
